title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1965 notes on the motivic Galois group. The preceding pages discuss full faithfulness of realization functors (Hodge/Tate-type statements). This page asks whether algebraic (motivic) de Rham classes can be characterized purely by Hodge-theoretic conditions: by the bigrading (Hodge type) or by reality.

Setup. Let K ⊂ C be a subfield, M a motive over K, and G its motivic Galois group, viewed as the Tannakian group of Betti realization T_B. The de Rham realization T_DR(M) is a K-vector space. The comparison isomorphism T_DR ⊗_K C ≅ T_B ⊗ C gives:
- a Hodge bigrading on T_DR(M)_C, whose (0,0) part Grothendieck writes T_DR(M)^{oo}_C;
- a real structure, from T_B ⊗ R.

The motivic invariants T_DR(M^G) = Hom(1,M) ⊗_Q K form a K-subspace of T_DR(M) with two properties:
(a) it lies in the (0,0) part;
(b) its (K∩R)-form Hom(1,M) ⊗ (K∩R) lies in the real subspace (T_DR(M)_C)_R.
Question: is there a converse, i.e. are the motivic (algebraic) classes exactly the de Rham classes satisfying (a) and/or (b)?

1° K = Q, G not connected: (a) and (b) together do not suffice. Take Artin motives (effective of weight 0), with G finite.
- (a) is vacuous, since everything is of type (0,0). So the converse of (a) holds only when G is trivial.
- For M = Q[G] attached to a Galois extension L/Q, T_DR(M) = L. An element x ∈ L is 'real' iff σ(x) ∈ R for every embedding σ. So (b) is satisfied by all of L exactly when L is totally real, while M^G = Q.
- Hence the converse fails, and one should restrict to connected G, or pass to K = Q̄ and use all embeddings K → C.

2° Converse of (a) alone is false even over Q̄. Twist G by the period torsor P = Isom_⊗(T_B ⊗ K, T_DR) to get the K-form G' = Aut_⊗(T_DR) = ad(P), with V' = P ×^{G_K} V and V_C ≅ V' ⊗_K C. The Hodge bigrading is a homomorphism (j1, j2): G_m × G_m → G'; this is essentially the Deligne-torus/Mumford–Tate cocharacter picture. For G commutative (CM motives), G' = G_K and the bigrading is defined over K. Let T be the image of (j1, j2).
- Then V'^T = T_DR ∩ (T_DR)^{oo}_C.
- T has dimension ≤ 2. So if G is a torus of dimension ≥ 3 (e.g. a CM abelian surface with a quartic CM field), there is a faithful representation of weight 0 with V'^T ≠ V'^{G'}.
- These are Q̄-rational de Rham classes of Hodge type (0,0) that are not motivic.

The next page leaves open a converse to (b) for algebraically closed K, using all embeddings K → C and possibly an extra condition (c).
errors: The transcribed sentence 'b) est vraie ssi L tot. réelle' only makes sense if read as: condition b) is satisfied by all of T_DR(M) = L (i.e. b) is vacuous) iff L is totally real. In that case the converse of b) fails as soon as [L:Q] > 1. As literally transcribed the logic is inverted.

In 2° the K-rationality of the torus T (and hence of V'^T as a K-subspace) is not automatic: in general the conjugate Hodge filtration is not defined over K. Grothendieck's restriction to commutative G (CM motives, where the Hodge splitting is defined over Q̄) is what makes the counterexample work. The phrase 'groupe de dim ≥ 3' should be read as 'torus of dim ≥ 3', because a 2-dimensional CM torus equals the image of G_m^2 and gives no counterexample.

The page tacitly uses that for non-CM motives (e.g. a non-CM elliptic curve) a single-embedding (0,0) condition on Q̄-de Rham classes may well cut out only the motivic classes. That depends on transcendence results (Chudnovsky, Wüstholz) not available in 1965, so the page cannot settle that case.

ideas.what: Hodge bigrading viewed as a homomorphism G_m × G_m → G' into the twisted (de Rham) form of the motivic Galois group
ideas.modern_name: Mumford–Tate group / Deligne torus S_C ≅ G_m^2 and Hodge cocharacter
ideas.where_published: Present in Saavedra Rivano's thesis (1972) and Deligne's later work; not in Grothendieck's own publications as far as I know

ideas.what: Period torsor P = Isom_⊗(T_B ⊗ K, T_DR) and the inner form G' = Aut_⊗(T_DR) = ad(P)
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of periods / de Rham motivic Galois group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture), developed by Deligne, André, Kontsevich
ideas.where_published: Period conjecture implicitly in the footnote of 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966); the torsor formulation appears in André's book (2004)

ideas.what: Characterizing motivic/algebraic de Rham classes by Hodge type and reality conditions, with counterexamples (Artin motives over Q; CM tori of dim ≥ 3 over Q̄)
ideas.modern_name: De Rham-rational Hodge classes, absolute Hodge classes, de Rham–Betti classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (absolute Hodge classes, 1982); André (de Rham–Betti structures)

ideas.what: Artin motive M = Q[G] with T_DR(M) = L; reality condition vacuous iff L totally real
ideas.modern_name: De Rham realization of Artin motives

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses, and leaves open, whether de Rham classes over an algebraically closed K that satisfy reality (and possibly further) conditions for ALL embeddings K → C, without any Betti-rationality requirement, are exactly the motivic classes. This is a variant of absolute-Hodge/algebraicity criteria using only de Rham data plus archimedean conditions; I do not know it as a standard formulated question.
missed.quote: Il faut donc se borner, si on cherche des réciproques pour le cas K ... K=Q̄ p.ex. ... envisager toutes les immersions K↪C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects with Grothendieck's period conjecture and de Rham–Betti classes (André, Bost–Charles). With the period conjecture, a criterion of this kind would follow for motives over Q̄. Explicit counterexamples or proofs for CM motives might be tractable.

deep.surprise_reason: In 1965 Grothendieck already treats the Hodge bigrading as a cocharacter G_m^2 → twisted motivic Galois group via the period torsor, and tests the characterization of algebraic de Rham classes by type and reality, with correct CM counterexamples. This anticipates Mumford–Tate, Deligne's absolute Hodge and André's de Rham–Betti viewpoints. The content is mostly reconstructible from later literature, though, and the open question is only sketched.
transcription_corrections: 'donc réc. de a) vraie en G=(e)' should probably read 'donc réc. de a) vraie ssi G=(e)'.
'b) est vraie ssi ... tot. réelle' likely reads 'b) est vide ssi ... tot. réelle' (vacuous condition).
'il suffit de prendre un groupe de dim ≥3' probably 'un tore de dim ≥3' (context: 'en G comm.').
'T_DR(M^G)' is the de Rham realization of the invariant submotive M^G; the inserted '= Hom(1,M) ⊗_Q K' is correct.
Title: 'classes de coh. D.R. essentiellement algébriques' seems right; the crossed-out word before it is illegible.
